title: Machine optimizer differential and benchmark corpus
objective: Build an independent generated/adversarial corpus and benchmark harness for bounded integers, binary64 arrays, prime residues, fixed extensions, and packed containers; include compile/cold/warm execution, copy/materialization/boundary metrics, CPython/O0 exact oracles, and held-out cubic profiler adapters without changing optimizer implementation or central manifests.

handoff.summary: Adds a deterministic 25-case generated/adversarial corpus spanning the five machine domains, independent JavaScript and CPython exact oracles, Sage.js O0/O2 differential checks, a five-domain compile/cold/warm benchmark with output-bit and boundary accounting, and adapters for the origin/class-group cubic profiler and matched Sage/PARI evidence. The corpus is intentionally detached from optimizer pass, lowering, and plugin identifiers so it can evaluate the centrally integrated implementations without sharing their assumptions.
risks: The full integration receipt is not yet green: after native Graph and FFLAS cache preparation resolved four missing-adapter failures, an overloaded shared host cancelled three unrelated hyperelliptic analytic-performance tests at their 180-second timeout in batch 8/27. Batches 1-7, including this lane's new integration-tier tests, passed.

The current frozen optimizer may consider its existing closed-ring region for some annotated bounded-integer and binary64 benchmark sources. The harness reports that detached IR without treating its IDs or selections as an oracle; integrated plugin priority and claim policy remain coordinator-owned.

The cubic profiler v1 evidence does not report copy or materialization counts. Its adapter preserves those fields as explicitly unavailable instead of inferring them, and preserves nested inclusive boundary timings without summing them.

Performance values documented here are diagnostic measurements from one contended Linux x64 host, not cross-platform ratchets. Platform ceilings require quiet-host linux-arm64, windows-x64, and macos-arm64 evidence after central plugin registration.
next_steps: Rerun the exact integration validation on an uncontended host and move this contract to review only after a fresh passing receipt exists.

Register the five domain plugins and their central lowering/verifier/dispatcher rows in the integration lane, then rerun this unchanged corpus and benchmark to obtain implementation-independent comparative evidence.
Capture origin/class-group cubic profiler evidence with both native and forced-JavaScript targets and pass each report through --cubic-profile.
Capture a matched origin/class-group Sage.js/PARI comparator report and pass it through --pari-evidence, keeping same-boundary phase ratios separate from whole-process totals.
Establish platform-specific performance ratchets only from repeated quiet-host captures after the integrated optimizer target choices stabilize.
